How the analysis differs from the paper's. Only monkey V is analysed, as the monkey L files mark no torque perturbation; the paper pools both monkeys except in its supplementary table. The response detection is one reading of the Methods (a threshold on the trial-averaged SDF set from the baseline's SD), with a t-test across trials as a variant. Its false-positive rate over the 200 ms epoch is 0.23, not the 0.01 the paper's threshold implies, and stationary Poisson spike trains give 0.16 to 0.21, most of it, so the claims that rest on the selection of responses are blocked, though their analyses ran. A threshold calibrated to a false-positive rate of 0.01 finds fewer torque-related cells, further from the paper's. With this detection the latency shortening after MPTP appears with the paper's monkey V means, but the response magnitudes fall after MPTP, which the paper did not find. The kinematic and EMG measures follow the Methods where they are given; the response windows, the EMG threshold and the peak velocity window are choices made here. The torque command differs in size between the states, so the kinematic and EMG differences found here cannot be attributed to MPTP, whatever their outcome on the criteria; compared at the same per-trial command step, movements are faster after MPTP for some steps and directions and slower for others. The m2 response can be compared at one step only (twice the smallest, 66 against 11 channel-sessions): its median over the triceps channels is smaller after MPTP (44.9 against 1.8), though on triceps longus 2 it is larger (52.2 against 113.0, 4 post-MPTP channel-sessions, p = 0.36), so a smaller m2 after MPTP rests on that one step and 11 post-MPTP channel-sessions. In synthetic tests the zero-phase filter, which the claims file fixes, moves a movement onset up to 14 ms earlier.

Changes after the first verification. The header now marks false-positive-rate and the 15 claims blocked by it as run and blocked. Added: the antidromic tests against their thresholds, a per-cell table of the detection, the position of the spike windows within the trials, the movement and EMG measures compared at the same per-trial command step, and the zero-phase filter on synthetic movements. The EMG threshold variants now keep responses lasting to the end of the window. No outcome changed.

Changes after the second verification. Text only: the m2 comparison at the same command step, the m2 by command size within each state, the false-positive rate against the paper's (about 23 and 46 times), and the cell-directions that can never respond are stated as the outputs show them. No outcome changed and none is proposed.

What changed from the earlier attempt (version 0.260518.1819). Every outcome is the same. The cell counts are no longer exactly the paper's (115 and 157 cells against 112 and 159), because the draft adds trials of second source files, so three pre-MPTP units now reach 5 perturbations per direction, and stores the two unit copies once; counting each unit from its first file gives the paper's pre-MPTP counts exactly. The session correlation of PTN latency with m2 no longer reaches the paper's threshold (p = 0.023, where it was 0.011). The other numbers moved by small amounts.

What was found about the dandiset, against the earlier attempt's findings.

  • Monkey L perturbations: still present. The monkey L files mark no torque perturbation (type not_available), the Leu torque command is NaN in every pre-MPTP file, and in the post-MPTP files it moves during the active movements, with one excursion in a hold window in 2048 trials. The draft's description now says the Leu files hold no perturbation times.
  • Analog clock: fixed. The analog streams share the trials' clock; the torque command steps 4 to 6 ms after every labelled onset on the stored clock.
  • Torque command sizes: partly fixed. The pulse is still about four times larger in most post-MPTP sessions than in most pre-MPTP sessions, with an opposite swing after MPTP and trial-to-trial variation; the torque description now says so, and that its scale is not known. The kinematic and EMG results differ between sessions of different command sizes.
  • Angle reference frame and series names: fixed. Positive is flexion, as the values show, and the monkey L series are named for the wrist.
  • Repeated files and unit copies: fixed. No file repeats another's trials, and each unit is stored once.
  • unit_also_in_session_id: fixed. The column is gone; units recorded across two files are one unit observed in both files' trials.
  • Dandiset description: fixed. It now says intracarotid MPTP, wrist movements for monkey L, and Leu recordings from August 1992 to December 1993, as the files do.
  • Sampling and EMG description: partly fixed. The EMG description now gives the paper's processing; the monkey L analog streams are still at 100 Hz (the paper says 200 Hz) and the EMG in A/D units, both now stated in the description.
  • Torque timing: still present, now stated in the description. The torque onset comes 1.70 to 1.73 s after the center target appears in 90% of perturbations, where the Methods describe an onset 1 to 2 s after center capture, at random.
  • New: three sessions (v1401, v1402, v1501) have labelled perturbations but no pulse in the torque command, as the torque description says.
  • New: the code that built the draft is in an open pull request of the conversion repository, not on its main branch, which the dandiset links.
  • The angle's scale agrees with the files' own movement amplitudes and peak velocities; the torque-induced movements (about 3 deg) are smaller than the paper's mean of 10 deg.
